about: Each vault secret's expiry date (PL-25), as Documents/Secrets-Register.md's rotation schedule gives it: how long after it is written its `exp` falls, as an ISO 8601 period, or "" for none. secrets.bicep compiles this file and sets attributes.exp on every secret a run writes, counted from the first day of the month it runs in (so Azure's what-if reads the same all month, and the infrastructure plan's hash holds from plan to Approve), and deploy.ts reads every expiry back after a secrets run (secret-expiry.ts). An expiry is informational: Key Vault still serves a secret past its `exp` (Microsoft, about-secrets), so a date only marks the end of a use period. A secret not written keeps the date it has: an app key gets its date when it is created (@onlyIfNotExists), and a written secret gets a new one with each new version. None for Zitadel's master key and machine-ID config (never rotated routinely), the first admin's starting password (used once; to be disabled instead), our login ID lists (not credentials) and the public halves (they rotate with their keys). The Zitadel tokens get a year from being written, which is the token's own expiry when it is pasted the day Zitadel issues it. `keys` is every app key's (`key-<purpose>-v<n>`), but the families in `keysNever`: the payee index is never rotated in place (ADR-014 §3).
